title: Can Yet More Sanctions Force Iran to Capitulate?
gist: A Warcast podcast episode with Alex Vatanka and Kerry Anderson examines a new Trump-administration sanctions offensive against Iran, questioning what is left to sanction and when additional measures might bite, and highlights Iran's trade with China and the UAE's move to suspend trade with Iran as pivotal factors.

insights.claim: The Trump administration announced new sanctions on Iran as part of what it describes as a major new economic offensive.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: A fresh sanctions escalation on Iran is a live geopolitical and oil-market catalyst.
insights.quote: new sanctions on Iran as part of what it says is a major new economic offensive
insights.locator: The Trump administration recently announced new sanctions

insights.claim: The effectiveness of further Iran sanctions is in doubt because much of Iran's economy has already been sanctioned, raising the question of what is left to target and when new measures would take effect.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Diminishing marginal impact of additional sanctions is key for pricing Iran-related oil and geopolitical risk.
insights.quote: what's left to sanction, when additional sanctions might have an effect

insights.claim: Iran's trade with China is cast as the crucial variable in any effort to further squeeze Iran's economy through sanctions.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Chinese purchases are the pressure valve that determines whether sanctions bite, so watch China-Iran oil flows.
insights.quote: why Iran's trade with China plays a crucial role in any effort to further squeeze the economy
insights.locator: why Iran's trade with China plays a crucial role

insights.claim: The United Arab Emirates has moved to suspend trade with Iran, tightening the regional economic pressure on Tehran.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: The UAE is a major re-export hub for Iran, so a suspension materially raises the cost of sanctions evasion.
insights.quote: the United Arab Emirates' move to suspend trade with Iran
